name: Luna 1
short_status: Missed its intended impact and flew past the Moon at 5,995 km on 4 Jan 1959, becoming the first spacecraft to escape Earth's gravity and orbit the Sun.
tagline: OKB-1 · Soviet Union · Flyby · 1959 · The space race Partial
stats: closest approach to the lunar surface
human-made object to escape Earth's gravity
distance of the glowing sodium-cloud beacon

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 2 January 1959, 16:41:21 UT, Tyuratam (Baikonur), on an 8K72 (no. B1-6)

facts.label: Intended mission
facts.value: Lunar impact, stated outright in NASA's Siddiqi chronicle (SP-2018-4041) from post-Soviet archives; fourth Ye-1 series attempt (three unannounced 1958 launch failures preceded it)

facts.label: Lunar flyby
facts.value: Within 5,995 km of the surface on 4 January 1959, about 34 hours after launch (NSSDCA; Siddiqi gives 6,400 km and notes some sources say up to 7,500 km)

facts.label: Sodium cloud experiment
facts.value: 1 kg of sodium released 3 January at 00:57 UT, 113,000 km from Earth; visible at magnitude ~6 over the Indian Ocean

facts.label: Key discoveries
facts.value: First direct observations of the solar wind; Moon found to have no magnetic field; new radiation-belt data

facts.label: Final orbit
facts.value: Heliocentric, between the orbits of Earth and Mars; nicknamed Mechta and Artificial Planet 1

timeline: Launch at 16:41:21 UT from Tyuratam (Baikonur) on an 8K72; first spacecraft to reach escape velocity
00:57 UT: 1 kg sodium cloud released 113,000 km from Earth; photographed by astronomers as a magnitude-6 orange glow
Flew past the Moon at 5,995 km after a guidance-system error spoiled the intended impact
Contact lost about 62 hours after launch; Luna 1 became the first artificial object in solar orbit
Retroactively renamed Luna 1 (originally announced as Cosmic Rocket)
